Subject: Post-signature: embedding the implementation plan into the MAP

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — we're excited to move forward. Before we sign the final SOW, our ops and security teams asked whether the post-signature implementation plan (rollout schedule, canary windows, migration cutover, and training milestones) can be embedded directly inside the MAP so we have a single source of truth.

Specifically can you:
- Provide a draft MAP with the embedded timeline and acceptance criteria.
- Call out the proposed canary window (preferred weekends, PST).
- List training sessions and target audiences (admin, support, engineering).
- Confirm rollback/fallback steps and who owns each step.

We're on a tight timetable — Harborline execs want an operational go/no-go decision by the week of July 9. Can we get a draft by EOD Wednesday (6/22)? I've attached the internal layout we've used previously.

[Attachment: Harborline_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Cheers,
Alex

Harborline Systems
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-signature: embedding the implementation plan into the MAP

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is our proposed MAP-embedded implementation plan (draft). High level summary below:

1) Canary plan (recommended approach)
   - Canary cohort: 5% traffic routed to Redwood inference variant A (quantized) for 48 hours.
   - Window options: Sat 7/14 - Sun 7/15 (PST) or Sat 7/21 - Sun 7/22.
   - Acceptance: 95th pct latency < 220ms, error rate < 0.5%, no output-regression on the included eval set.

2) Migration/cutover
   - Dry-run migration window: Thu 7/26 (internal validation).
   - Live cutover: Mon 7/30 (low-traffic morning), with phased traffic ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100% across 8 hours).
   - Rollback: immediate traffic switch to previous model pool + hotfix route to hosted fallback if anomaly detected. Owners: Harborline infra (cut), Redwood runbook (assist).

3) Training schedule
   - Admin ops training: 2 sessions (7/17, 7/19) 90 mins — runbooks, monitoring, incident playbooks.
   - Engineering handover: deep-dive (7/20) 2 hours — KV cache behavior, token accounting.
   - Support enablement: 60-min quickstart (7/24) with triage checklist.

4) Acceptance & handoff checklist (embedded in MAP)
   - Eval pass (automated prompts), smoke test pass, security checklist complete, runbook accepted by Harborline oncall.

I've annotated the draft with versioned acceptance criteria and left inline comments where we recommend a 10% pre-go discount credit (standard) for close-by go-live commitment.

[Attachment: MAP_Draft_EmbeddedPlan_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

I'll follow up with a succinct mutual action items doc that you can add to your internal tracker.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

This is very helpful, thanks. Quick items from ops/legal:

- Harborline execs asked about a modest commercial incentive if Redwood can commit to the earlier canary weekend (7/14-7/15). I looped Ben Carter from RD so we can fast-track approvals.
